Title: L&G shareholders approve higher FY26 dividend
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Land & General Bhd's shareholders have approved all nine resolutions at the group's 63rd annual general neeting (AGM) today.
Among the resolutions approved was a single-tier final dividend of 0.8 sen per share for the financial year ended March 31, 2026 (FY26).
Together with the first interim dividend of 0.2 sen per share paid on May 7, the company's total dividend for FY26 amounts to 1.0 sen per share, 25 per cent higher than the 0.8 sen paid for FY25.
The final dividend will be paid on Oct 16 to entitled shareholders.
Shareholders also approved the re-election of three directors, reappointment of KPMG PLT as auditors, general authority to allot and issue shares and the proposed share buy-back.
The dividends particularly come after a record FY26, with group revenue surging 70.6 per cent to RM490.5 million, while pre-tax profit rose 25.6 per cent to RM74.2 million.
The momentum strengthened in Q1 FY27, with revenue jumping 61.5 per cent year-on-year to RM159 million and pre-tax profit climbing 42.6 per cent to RM24.9 million.
As at June 30 this year, L&G recorded RM513 million in unbilled sales, providing continued earnings visibility as construction progresses, supported by about RM1.5 billion in planned launches for FY27.
Managing director Low Gay Teck said the support received at today's AGM reinforces L&G's commitment to deliver sustainable returns while continuing to position the group for long-term growth.
"We will continue to build on the strong operating momentum achieved in FY26 and the first quarter of FY27."
Beyond its current financial performance, the company is also embarking on a strategic evolution to broaden its growth platform.
Property development remains its core earnings driver, supported by a healthy pipeline of residential projects and disciplined execution.
Central to the group's industrial growth strategy is the proposed transformation of the group's approximately Lembah Beringin landbank into an industrial park.
Subject to the necessary approvals, the first phase is targeted for launch within FY27, with revenue recognition expected to commence from FY28.
"Our move into industrial park development is an expansion of L&G's capabilities, not a departure from the strengths we have built over decades.
"Property development will continue to anchor the group, education will provide recurring earnings, and industrial development will open a new avenue for long-term growth.
"Together, these three pillars give L&G broader and more resilient platform for the future," added Low.

Title: Malaysia reaffirms close partnership with Philippines
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has reaffirmed its close partnership with the Philippines, with cooperation in Asean, trade and investment, and peacebuilding in Mindanao continuing to serve as key pillars of bilateral relations.
Malaysian Ambassador to the Philippines Datuk Abdul Malik Melvin Castelino said Malaysia strongly supported the Philippines' 2026 Asean chairmanship under the theme "Navigating Our Future, Together", particularly as the regional grouping begins implementing the Asean 2045: Our Shared Future vision.
Speaking at a reception marking Malaysia's 69th National Day in Manila on Monday, he said Malaysia was proud to see its close neighbour carry forward Asean's work at an important time for the region.
"We are proud to see our close neighbour carry forward the work of Asean at an important moment for the region," he said, adding that Malaysia supported the Philippines' focus on peace and security, shared prosperity and the empowerment of its people.
Abdul Malik said Asean cooperation was particularly important in strengthening regional resilience amid conflicts and challenges, including developments in West Asia, Palestine and Gaza, as well as Europe, which had caused immense humanitarian suffering and displacement.
"We hope that all parties involved continue to push for peace and stability through dialogue and mediation in the tradition of Asean," he said.
On Malaysia-Philippines ties, he described the relationship as deep, practical and people-centred, underpinned by shared geography, history, culture, family connections and a common interest in maintaining a peaceful and prosperous neighbourhood.
"The close engagement between Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. has further strengthened the positive momentum in our relations," he said.
He said cooperation spanned trade and investment, the digital economy, education, tourism, halal cooperation, culture, connectivity and people-to-people exchanges.
The ambassador also reaffirmed Malaysia's commitment to supporting peace and development in Mindanao and the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM), congratulating the Philippines and the people of BARMM on the recently concluded election.
"We believe that lasting peace must be accompanied by economic opportunity, strong institutions and confidence in a better future," he said, stressing that progress in Mindanao contributed to the peace, stability and prosperity of the wider region.
Meanwhile, the Embassy of Malaysia in Manila said in a statement that the reception brought together senior Philippine government officials, members of the diplomatic corps, business leaders and partners from various sectors.
It said the event highlighted cooperation in Asean, trade and investment, peacebuilding in Mindanao, tourism, education and people-to-people ties.
Referring to Palestine, Abdul Malik said lasting peace must be grounded in justice, respect for international law and the equal dignity of all peoples, while emphasising the importance of dialogue, diplomacy and the peaceful settlement of disputes.
He said Malaysia and the Philippines, as close neighbours and fellow Asean members, were bound not only by geography but also by shared values, common aspirations and strong people-to-people ties.
He expressed confidence that the 2 countries would continue working together towards a more peaceful, prosperous and resilient region.

Title: EC awaits official notice on Melaka state assembly dissolution
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Election Commission (EC) has yet to receive official notification regarding the dissolution of the Melaka state legislative assembly.
Its chairman, Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun, said a special meeting regarding the state election will be held as soon as the official notification is received.
"The EC takes note of the announcement on the dissolution of the Melaka state assembly, which takes effect tomorrow.
"We may hold a special meeting regarding this election once we receive the official notification of the dissolution from the Melaka Speaker," he said to TV3's Buletin Utama.
Ramlan said the meeting will determine key dates for the state election, including nomination day and early voting.
Earlier today,
Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh
announced that the Melaka state assembly will be dissolved tomorrow.
He said Yang di-Pertua Negeri Melaka Tun Dr Mohd Ali Mohd Rustam had consented to the dissolution following an audience earlier.
The move ends weeks of speculation over when the assembly would be dissolved.

Title: Lawyer: State executive council has no power to suspend Negri top officials
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A lawyer has described the suspension of the Negri Sembilan state secretary and state legal adviser by the state executive council (MMKN) as invalid and without legal effect.
Lawyer Muhammad Hariz Md Yusoff said the MMKN had no authority over the services of the state secretary and state Legal Adviser, and that the special meeting at which the decision was made was also invalid.
He said the appointments of the state secretary and state legal adviser were made by the Public Service Commission rather than the menteri besar or MMKN.
He called on the Chief Secretary to the Government, Public Service Department (PSD) and Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) not to give effect to the suspension notices, arguing that they were issued by a body without jurisdiction.
"Article 144(1) of the Federal Constitution places the power to appoint, promote, transfer and exercise disciplinary control over members of the public service with the relevant service commission.
"Suspension from duty is an administrative and disciplinary action. It can only be taken by the lawful disciplinary authority. MMKN is not the service commission and is not the disciplinary authority.
"Therefore, we maintain our position that state secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim and state legal adviser Datuk Muzalmah Mustapha Kamal remain lawfully in their respective positions at all relevant times," he said in a statement.
Earlier today,
Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail
Lasim said the state government has suspended Zafir Muzalmah with immediate effect.
He said state financial officer Datuk Masri Razali would perform the duties of state secretary until a new state secretary is appointed by the Chief Secretary to the Government.
Meanwhile, lawyer Fahmi Adilah will provide legal advice until a new state legal adviser is appointed by the A-GC.
Hariz said the fact that the suspension notices would be sent to the Chief Secretary to the Government, PSD and A-GC was itself a clear indication that authority over the two positions rested with other parties, rather than MMKN.
He said a party without the power to appoint individuals to the two positions could not arbitrarily suspend them.
"Civil servants are placed under the PSD so that they can act in accordance with the law without fear or favour.
"Taking action against officers for complying with the A-GC's advice undermines that foundation. Any power, even if it exists, that is exercised for an improper purpose could be declared invalid," he said.
He said civil servants in the state should continue to receive instructions through the lawful state secretary and legal advice from the lawful state legal adviser.
He added that actions taken based on instructions from those appointed under today's resolution could be subject to legal challenges and expose officers to disciplinary risks.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Perodua, Bank Rakyat roll out co-branded credit card
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Perusahaan Otomobil Kedua Sdn Bhd (Perodua) and Bank Rakyat have launched a co-branded credit card that offers special benefits for automotive-related spending.
The Perodua-Bank Rakyat Credit Card-i is designed to meet vehicle owners' needs by offering reward points that can be easily transferred and redeemed through the Perodua P-Circle app.
Among the special features offered by the card are reward points for spending on fuel, electric vehicle (EV) charging, vehicle maintenance and takaful protection purchases.
The credit card also offers zero per cent overseas transaction fees and no annual fee for cardholders.
Perodua president and chief executive officer (CEO) Datuk Seri Zainal Abidin Ahmad said it was the first time the company partnered with a banking institution to issue credit cards.
"We will also conduct a special campaign to encourage our customers to obtain this credit card-i through exclusive Perodua package offers," he said.
Bank Rakyat group CEO Ahmad Shahril Mohd Shariff said the strategic partnership with Perodua reflected Bank Rakyat's approach to building an ecosystem that provides customers with more comprehensive value and rewards.
"This initiative is in line with Bank Rakyat's 'Untuk Semua' (For Everyone) aspiration to expand access to inclusive and relevant financial solutions for all segments of society.
"We believe partnerships such as this can create more opportunities for Bank Rakyat to expand its reach, strengthen the customer experience, and develop more innovative and value-added Shariah-compliant financial solutions," he said.

Title: Indonesia braces for forest, land fire risk into early October as El Nino keeps rainfall low
Article:
JAKARTA: The risk of forest and land fires is expected to persist in parts of Indonesia into early October, with a very strong El Nino forecast to prolong dry conditions and keep rainfall generally low across much of the country.
The Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) said relatively dry atmospheric conditions remained particularly evident in parts of Sumatra and Kalimantan, where high concentrations of hotspots have been detected over the past 10 days alongside reports of forest and land fires.
The agency said as of Sept 21, Central Kalimantan recorded the highest concentration, with 5,283 hotspots, followed by South Sumatra with 1,485 and West Kalimantan with 1,357, while hundreds more were detected in South and East Kalimantan.
"As dry conditions strengthen, the public and regional governments are urged to conserve water and increase vigilance against the threat of drought and forest and land fires," it said in a statement.
BMKG forecast rainfall across most of Indonesia to remain at low to moderate levels from late September into early October, although localised heavy rain could still occur as short-term atmospheric conditions promote rain-cloud formation in some regions.
In its 2026-2027 rainy season outlook, BMKG said more than 60 per cent of Indonesia's land area is expected to see the rainy season begin later than the long-term average for the respective regions, with many areas entering the season in November or December.
Its Deputy for Climatology Ardhasena Sopaheluwakan said the rainy season was also forecast to be shorter than usual across more than half of the country's land area, although this did not necessarily mean rainfall would be lower throughout the season.
"Although it is predicted to be shorter, the 2026/2027 rainy season is generally expected to have normal rainfall," he said in a separate statement, adding that some areas could receive above-normal rainfall while a smaller proportion is forecast to be drier than usual.
BMKG said much of Indonesia is expected to reach the peak of its rainy season between December and February, although the timing varies across the vast archipelago.
It also urged authorities to improve drainage systems and evacuation preparedness for floods and landslides at the onset and peak of the rainy season, as the country prepares for an eventual shift from prolonged dry conditions to increased rainfall.

Title: Ansara members get extra RM5,000 discount on selected PR1MA homes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The first 200 members of the Association of Former Students of Mara Junior Science College (Ansara) or their family members who purchase selected Perbadanan PR1MA Malaysia (PR1MA) homes will receive an additional RM5,000 discount.
PR1MA said the incentive was part of a cooperation agreement signed with Ansara today to expand access to its homeownership opportunities and initiatives for Ansara members and their families.
In a statement, PR1MA said the collaboration would include homeownership awareness programmes, briefing and engagement sessions, information sharing on housing and PR1MA promotions, as well as referral programmes and joint communication initiatives.
The RM5,000 incentive is offered alongside the Rumah PR1MA Kita and Rumah PR1MA Kita+ campaigns, as well as other promotional campaigns approved by PR1MA, subject to applicable terms, eligibility and current unit availability.
PR1MA group chief executive officer Brian Iskandar Zulkarim and Ansara president Taufiq Hussien signed the agreement during a ceremony at PR1MA's headquarters.
Brian Iskandar said the collaboration reflected PR1MA's commitment to expanding access to homeownership through a network of organisations and communities.
"Through Ansara's extensive network, this partnership allows PR1MA to reach more prospective homebuyers directly. We hope the benefits offered will help Ansara members and their families take a step closer to owning their own homes," he said.
Meanwhile, Taufiq said the collaboration was part of Ansara's efforts to provide its members and their families with relevant benefits, particularly in helping them plan for homeownership.
"Homeownership is an important commitment in a person's life. Therefore, we welcome the collaboration with PR1MA, which not only gives Ansara members access to housing options, but also offers additional benefits to assist them in planning to own a home," he said.
PR1MA said it would continue to explore strategic partnerships with various organisations and associations to create more opportunities for Malaysians to own quality and affordable homes.
PR1MA is the lead agency under the Housing and Local Government Ministry responsible for providing affordable housing for the M40 group.

Title: Thailand on alert as Chao Phraya river water levels expected to rise
Article:
BANGKOK: Thailand has stepped up preparedness and round-the-clock monitoring of water levels in the Chao Phraya river as an increased water flow is forecast from Sept 29.
Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation (DDPM) director-general Theeraphat Kachamat said 10 central provinces and Bangkok had been ordered to closely monitor the situation following a forecast by the Royal Irrigation Department that water flow at Station C.2 in Muang district, Nakhon Sawan, is expected to reach 1,400 to 1,450 cubic metres per second on Sept 29.
According to DDPM, the provinces are Uthai Thani, Chai Nat, Sing Buri, Ang Thong, Suphan Buri, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, Lop Buri, Pathum Thani, Nonthaburi and Samut Prakan.
However, Theeraphat said the forecast water levels were not expected to affect communities located within designated flood embankment lines.
The DDPM also urged urgent dissemination of warnings to residents living along both banks of the Chao Phraya and Noi rivers, as well as private-sector operators conducting activities along the waterways.
"These include operators involved in flood-protection embankment construction and floating restaurants, who have been advised to closely monitor developments and prepare to move belongings and equipment to higher ground for safety," he said.
Local authorities and relevant agencies have also been instructed to inspect the stability of flood embankments, prepare disaster-response machinery and ensure personnel are on standby. - BERNAMA

Title: Sarawak state assembly's final sitting likely in October — Speaker
Article:
KUCHING: The Sarawak state assembly's sitting next month is expected to be the final sitting of its current term, said Speaker Tan Sri Mohamad Asfia Awang Nassar.
He said further details on the sitting, including the list of Bills to be tabled, would be announced at a press conference a day before the sitting begins.
"I will hold a press conference a day before the state assembly sitting and, of course, this will be the final sitting because the current term will end after that.
"So far, my office has yet to receive any Bills from the state government," he told reporters after officiating the Aku Kasih Malaysia: Sarawak Youth Leadership seminar here today.
The current term of the Sarawak state assembly will end in February 2027.

Title: Public urged to stay calm after weak 4.4-magnitude quake off Batu Pahat
Article:
BATU PAHAT: The public have been advised to remain calm and refrain from spreading unverified information following a weak 4.4-magnitude earthquake detected off Batu Pahat this evening.
Batu Pahat district officer Mohd Farid Kassim said the public should refer to the latest updates from reliable sources, including the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) website.
Farid, who is also the district Disaster Management Committee chairman, said
MetMalaysia reported that
the weak earthquake occurred at 4.55pm.
He said initial reports indicated that tremors could be felt in several areas around Batu Pahat and nearby areas.
"MetMalaysia and relevant agencies are monitoring the situation from time to time to ensure conditions in Batu Pahat remain safe, particularly for the public.
"The public are also advised to report any emergency incidents to the authorities, including the police, mukim penghulu or local community leaders.
"The Batu Pahat District Disaster Management Committee will continue to provide the latest updates from time to time to ensure the safety and well-being of the community," he said in a statement.
Earlier, MetMalaysia said in a statement that the weak earthquake occurred about 27km southwest of Batu Pahat, at a depth of 10km.

Title: Thai Customs seize RM870,000 hidden in vehicle at Sadao border
Article:
KOTA BARU: Thai Customs have seized RM870,000 in Malaysian currency concealed inside a vehicle entering Thailand through the Sadao border checkpoint on Sunday.
A Thai security spokesman said a man was arrested for possessing the money.
He said the seizure was made following information gathered through intelligence and investigations.
"Customs officers from the Customs Control Division, Regional Customs Office 4 and Sadao Customs inspected the Thai-registered vehicle and found the cash concealed inside.
"The cash, estimated to be worth about 7.1 million baht, was seized under Section 166 of the Thai Customs Act 2017.
"The owner or possessor may face charges under Section 242 read with Section 252 of the same Act," he said.
The spokesman said the case had been handed over to Sadao Customs for further legal action.
"Thai authorities are still conducting further investigations, including into the purpose of the cash being brought into Thailand," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SCIB proposes ESOS of up to 15pct of issued shares to key personnel
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sarawak Consolidated Industries Bhd (SCIB) has announced a proposed employees' share option scheme (ESOS) involving up to 15 per cent of its total issued share capital.
The incentive scheme, detailed alongside the group's proposed property diversification announcement, could see up to 114.54 million new ordinary shares issued to eligible directors and employees over a five-year period.
In an announcement to Bursa today, SCIB's board is seeking shareholder approval at an upcoming extraordinary general meeting (EGM) to grant up to 80 per cent of the ESOS directly to key executive leaders, notably its chief executive officer (CEO) Michael Tan Thian Zhi and chief operating officer (COO) Huang Vui Bing.
Tan, who was appointed as CEO on May 29, and Huang, (appointed COO on May 22), currently hold zero shares in SCIB.
The exercise price of the ESOS options will be calculated based on a discount of not more than 10 per cent against the 5-day volume-weighted average market price of SCIB shares prior to the offer date.
If fully exercised at the illustrative price of 11.1 sen per share, the scheme will generate RM12.71 million in fresh cash proceeds.
Management intends to utilize these proceeds entirely as working capital to fund day-to-day operations, administrative expenses, and staff payroll associated with its expanding property operations.
Alongside the ESOS announcement, SCIB is seeking shareholder approval to diversify into property development, aiming to establish a new growth engine following the sale of its core manufacturing business earlier this year.
In the same announcement, its principal adviser Berjaya Securities Sdn Bhd announced that SCIB intends to build a pipeline of residential, commercial, and industrial projects across Sarawak and Sabah.
The proposed diversification is anticipated to contribute 25 per cent or more of SCIB's net profits moving forward.
The move follows the completion of SCIB's RM113 million cash disposal of its wholly-owned unit, SCIB Concrete Manufacturing Sdn Bhd (SCM), to YTL Cement (Sarawak) Sdn Bhd on May 22.
The exit from precast concrete manufacturing left SCIB operating primarily through its construction and engineering segment. To broaden its earnings base, SCIB is reallocating part of the SCM disposal proceeds to fund its property ventures.
SCIB's initial development portfolio targets key growth centers in Bintulu, Sarawak as well as  Penampang and Kota Kinabalu in Sabah.

Title: UPNM, Ketech Asia to commercialise palm oil-based explosives technology
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is moving to commercialise locally developed palm oil-based technology for the production of explosives and ammunition in a bid to strengthen the country's defence supply chain and reduce reliance on imports.
Universiti Pertahanan Nasional Malaysia (UPNM) has signed a memorandum of agreement (MoA) with Ketech Asia Sdn Bhd to bring the university's locally developed technology from the laboratory stage towards large-scale production for use by the defence and security industries.
The agreement was signed in conjunction with the University Research, Innovation and Investment Summit (URIIS) 2026 organised by the Higher Education Ministry today.
The signing was witnessed by Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir.
Under the collaboration, the technology will be developed from Technology Readiness Level 3 (TRL 3), representing the laboratory stage, to TRL 8 or 9, where it would be ready for large-scale production and deployment within the defence and security sectors.
UPNM vice-chancellor Lt Gen Datuk Arman Rumaizi Ahmad said taking the technology from the laboratory to a market-ready stage would require investment, access to specialised testing facilities and industry expertise recognised locally and internationally.
"The partnership will enable the fabrication of full-scale prototypes, field testing and standards certification for dual-use technology to be carried out in a more structured and sustainable manner," he said.
UPNM said developing explosive materials from local biological resources such as palm oil demonstrated the ability of public university researchers to harness domestic resources to strengthen Malaysia's strategic supply chain.
The commercialisation initiative is also aimed at improving the country's defence and security preparedness while generating socioeconomic benefits through the creation of highly skilled jobs and reducing dependence on imported materials.
During the event, Zahid and Zambry also visited UPNM's Defence Technology, Strategy and Security Cluster booth, which showcased several university innovations ready for commercialisation.
UPNM said URIIS 2026 served as a platform to strengthen cooperation between government policy, university research capabilities and industry investment, with the aim of translating research funding into economic and national security benefits.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze-related illnesses decline, asthma cases down 35.36pct
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The number of haze-related illness cases declined in Epidemiological Week (EW) 37/2026, with asthma cases registering the largest drop of 35.36 per cent from the previous week, according to the Health Ministry (MOH).
In a statement today, the MOH said daily monitoring at 78 haze-specific sentinel health facilities nationwide recorded 722 asthma cases in EW 37/2026, down by 395 cases from 1,117 in EW 36/2026.
Conjunctivitis cases also fell by 32.04 per cent, or 107 cases, from 334 to 227 during the same period.
Meanwhile, upper respiratory tract infection (URTI) cases dropped by 1,426, or 20.18 per cent, from 7,065 to 5,639.
"Despite the decline in monitored haze-related illnesses, the MOH will continue to closely monitor the haze situation and its health impacts, particularly in areas recording 'Unhealthy' air quality levels," the statement read.
The ministry said measures included daily monitoring of URTI, asthma and conjunctivitis cases at 78 haze-specific sentinel health facilities, as well as assessing API readings alongside health surveillance data to determine appropriate public health measures.
It added that the National Haze Operations Room, activated on Sept 4, would continue to coordinate monitoring and response efforts while ensuring health facilities remained prepared, including through the availability of medicines, oxygen supplies and relevant medical equipment.
The MOH also advised the public, particularly those in areas with unhealthy air quality, to reduce outdoor activities and postpone strenuous physical exertion.
It urged high-risk groups, including children, the elderly and those with chronic respiratory or heart conditions, to take the necessary precautions.
As of 7am today, 16 stations recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, with 10 in Sarawak, two in Selangor, and one each in Putrajaya, Kuala Lumpur, Negri Sembilan and Sabah.
A total of 50 stations recorded moderate API readings, while two recorded good air quality. None recorded "very unhealthy" or "hazardous" readings.

Title: Charges against five Stanford pro-Palestinian protesters to be dismissed
Article:
WASHINGTON: Charges against five former and current Stanford University students will be dismissed in relation to a 2024 pro-Palestinian demonstration in which protesters barricaded themselves inside the school president's office.
California Attorney General Rob Bonta's office said on Monday it would dismiss the charges if the five defendants completed 100 hours of community service each and paid about US$52,000 combined in restitution to the university.
Santa Clara County Deputy Public Defender Avi Singh, who represented one of the defendants, said all had "made full restitution and agreed to complete substantial community service so they can move forward with their lives," according to the San Francisco Chronicle.
A judge declared a mistrial in February in the case after jurors could not reach a verdict. Twelve protesters were initially charged with felony vandalism. Seven of them previously accepted plea deals or diversion programmes.
Prosecutors said at the time the charges were filed that at least one suspect entered the building by breaking a window. Police arrested 13 people on June 5, 2024, in relation to the incident and the university said the building sustained "extensive" damage.
The charges were among the most serious against participants in the 2024 pro-Palestinian protest movement on US colleges in which demonstrators demanded an end to Israeli attacks and strikes on Gaza and to Washington's support for its ally, along with a divestment of funds by their universities from companies supporting Israel.
Protesters had renamed the building "Dr Adnan's Office" after Adnan Al-Bursh, a Palestinian doctor who died in an Israeli prison after months of detention.
Over 3,000 people were arrested during the 2024 US pro-Palestinian protest movement, according to media tallies. Some students faced suspension, expulsion and the revocation of their degrees.
After the mistrial, Santa Clara County District Attorney Jeff Rosen said he would seek a new trial. However, defence attorneys were able to successfully argue that his office should be removed from the case, citing concerns including his past remarks. The California attorney general's office took over the case.-REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sarawak hopes MA63 commitments reflected in 2027 Budget – Abang Johari
Article:
KUCHING: Sarawak hopes funding-related matters agreed under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) will be reflected in the 2027 Budget.
Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Abang Openg said the state government hoped the federal government would continue implementing matters agreed upon under MA63.
"Our hope is that what has been discussed under MA63, particularly in terms of funding, can be implemented," he said when met after officiating the Sarawak state-owned companies (SOE) Transformation Programme.
Asked whether Sarawak expected an increase in allocations under the 2027 Budget, Abang Johari said the matter would depend on the Prime Minister's announcement on Oct 9.
"We will see what the Prime Minister announces," he said.
Meanwhile, Abang Johari hinted that the state government was planning to review funding for several SOEs.
However, he declined to disclose the number of SOEs identified for funding cuts, instead asking all parties to wait for the tabling of the Sarawak 2027 Budget.
"Wait for the Budget. How can I reveal the Budget? This is not the Budget (announcement)," he said.
Asked whether the move involved several SOEs, Abang Johari confirmed that it was part of the state government's direction and policy.
"Later... we have already mentioned this and, as I explained earlier, it is the direction and policy. Wait for the Budget first," he said.

Title: More than 10,000 could flee Yemen fighting to Djibouti: UN
Article:
GENEVA: Renewed fighting in Yemen could see the number of refugees fleeing across the Red Sea to Djibouti jump to 10,000, while displacement inside Yemen could swell to over 230,000, the UN warned Tuesday.
The Iran-backed Houthis earlier this month seized control of Yemen's Red Sea coastline, in a dramatic offensive that has left hundreds of people on both sides dead, threatened global trade and pushed up energy prices.
The latest fighting between the Houthis and forces loyal to the Aden-based government, backed by Saudi Arabia, has sparked a fresh humanitarian crisis.
More than 100,000 civilians have been uprooted inside Yemen while others have risked dangerous sea crossings to flee the violence.
"Intensifying fighting in Yemen could drive more mass displacement," United Nations refugee agency spokesman Babar Baloch told reporters in Geneva.
Already, more than 3,000 people have fled across the Red Sea to Djibouti in the space of a week. UNHCR said it was bracing for that number to rise significantly, especially after mid-October when the current difficult sea conditions are expected to improve.
The agency and its partners are now "planning for more than 10,000 arrivals in Djibouti" in the coming months, Baloch said.
At the same time, the number of people displaced within Yemen by the recent fighting could swell from more than 130,000 today to over 230,000 people, he said.
That comes on top of the more than 5.2 million people who were already internally displaced in Yemen before the fighting reignited.
Baloch warned that the renewed conflict was deepening an already dire crisis in Yemen, where an estimated 22 million people require humanitarian assistance.
He warned that a severe funding shortfall was hampering the response to the emergency, with UNHCR's Yemen operation currently just 18 per cent funded for 2026.
The agency estimated that US$25 million is urgently needed to provide around 231,000 people with immediate aid.
UNHCR's Djibouti operations are meanwhile only 15-per cent funded, with the agency appealing for US$13.5 million "to ensure arrivals can access registration, reception, protection and other essential services."--AFP

Title: Sum Technology buys 51pct of security solutions firm INI Technologies for RM2mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sum Technology Bhd is acquiring a 51 per cent stake in security and automation specialist INI Technologies Sdn Bhd for RM2 million cash, expanding beyond its core engineering business.
In a Bursa Malaysia filing, the cleanroom and engineering solutions provider said it had entered into a share sale agreement for the acquisition, which will be funded entirely through internally generated funds.
The deal will give Sum Technology access to INI Technologies' electronic security, video surveillance and analytics, access control and automation capabilities.
It will also provide opportunities to cross-sell services to both companies' customers and expand Sum Technology's presence on the East Coast, where INI Technologies has operated in Kuantan for about 20 years.
Sum Technology executive director and chief executive officer Lee Thiam Hing said the acquisition would broaden the group's capabilities as industrial facilities and data centres become increasingly digitalised.
"As industrial facilities, data centres and other mission-critical environments become increasingly digitalised, we see opportunities to integrate our engineering capabilities with technologies such as video analytics, intelligent monitoring, access control and automated systems," he said in a statement.
Lee said INI Technologies' technical expertise and relationships with technology partners complemented Sum Technology's mechanical, electrical, process utilities and fire fighting (MEPF) engineering capabilities.
"By combining our MEPF engineering capabilities with INI Technologies' electronic security, video analytics and automation expertise, we see opportunities to develop more integrated solutions that enable facilities to monitor, analyse and respond more intelligently to their operating environments.
"Over time, we intend to build on these capabilities and explore greater adoption of AI-enabled video analytics, intelligent monitoring and automation applications," he said.
As at Aug 18, INI Technologies had 20 ongoing projects worth a combined RM3.27 million, with about RM1.58 million remaining to be billed.
The acquisition is expected to be completed by the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to the fulfilment or waiver of conditions under the agreement. INI Technologies will then become a 51 per cent-owned subsidiary of Sum Technology.

Title: Malay reserve land gazetted out for SABDA development to be replaced – Selangor MB
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The 55.401-acre (about 22.4ha) Malay reserve land in Tanjong Karang, Sabak Bernam, gazetted out for the development of the Sabak Bernam Development Area (SABDA), will be replaced with a tract of the same size in Hulu Selangor.
Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the move was aimed at striking a balance between development needs and the preservation of Malay reserve land.
He said the 55.401-acre plot in Tanjong Karang, Sabak Bernam, was gazetted out on Sept 3 specifically for the development of SABDA.
"SABDA is an initiative by the Selangor state government to develop the northern part of the state to strengthen food security and realise the potential of agro-tourism along the west coast, while creating more job opportunities for locals.
"The initiative is led by the state government-owned Menteri Besar Selangor Incorporated (MBI) and also involves local communities, including fishermen, entrepreneurs and academics.
"To achieve a balance between local development and the interests of Malay reserve land, a tract of the same size, 55.401 acres, in Hulu Selangor is also undergoing the gazettement process," he said in a statement today.
Amirudin said the total area of Malay reserve land in Selangor had increased by 2,680 acres since 2018 under the current state administration, compared with the previous administration.
He said the area had increased from 400,711 acres (about 162,161ha) to 403,391 acres (about 163,246ha).

Title: 2027 Budget: Higher allowances proposed for PDK trainers, disabled workers
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The Women, Family and Community Development Ministry (KPWKM) has proposed higher allowances for disabled workers and staff at Community Rehabilitation Centres (PDK) under the 2027 Budget.
Its minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the ministry was committed to ensuring that persons with disabilities (PwD) and those involved in caregiving received appropriate support, particularly to improve their quality of life.
"Regarding the allowances for PDK trainers, we have proposed increasing them, but approval has not yet been given. We have to wait for the budget announcement to know whether it will be approved.
"Most PDKs depend on external donations and support from elected representatives in their respective areas. That is why elected representatives often raise the matter and call for higher allowances to help the communities they serve," she said.
She said this at a press conference after officiating the closing ceremony of the Able for Disable Programme and the presentation of certificates for the Aeon Job Coach Introduction Course 2026.
Nancy said ahead of the tabling of the 2027 Budget, her ministry also hoped its proposal to strengthen the care economy would be approved.
"We want it to become a successful programme for those in need, including PwD and those caring for PwD, so we hope the proposals we have made will receive approval," she said.
In her speech at the event, Nancy urged all parties to move beyond simply employing PwD towards developing their talents and careers.
She said the private sector had a significant role to play given the abundance of employment opportunities available, and urged employers to assess the potential and contributions that PwD could offer.
"At the same time, I urge organisations to involve the PwD community itself in planning an inclusive work environment and employment system. The principle is simple: we should not assume what PwD need without listening to their own experiences.
"In KPWKM's accessibility agenda, the PwD community is also emphasised as users and partners who must be involved in evaluating the solutions developed, because the true measure of inclusivity is the experience of those who use the system," she said.

Title: MMAG proposes RM130mil capital reduction to erase accumulated losses
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MMAG Holdings Bhd has announced a proposed share capital reduction of up to RM130 million to eliminate its accumulated losses and rationalise its financial position, M&A Securities Sdn Bhd, acting as the principal adviser to the group, announced on Sept 22.
MMAG stated that rationalising its financial position will allow its balance sheet to better reflect the value of its underlying assets, thereby improving its profile and standing among commercial bankers, customers, suppliers, and investors.
As of March 31, 2026, MMAG's accumulated losses stood at RM106.77 million. Assuming the maximum credit arising from the capital reduction were set off against the group's accumulated losses, MMAG will record retained earnings of RM23.06 million.
The proposed reduction will not alter MMAG's current share price, the total number of issued shares, or shareholder equity proportions, nor will it involve any cash outflow or capital distribution to shareholders.
As of Sept 11, 2026, MMAG's issued share capital stood at RM298.3 million comprising 2.32 billion ordinary shares, alongside 101.19 million outstanding warrants with an exercise price of 15 sen apiece that are set to expire on Jan 15, 2029.
The capital restructuring coincides with improvements in the group's business over the 18-month period ended March 31, 2026 (FP26). During the period, MMAG saw its revenue expand 59.6 per cent to RM1.32 billion, compared with RM824.37 million in the preceding 18-month period ended Sept 30, 2024.
The increase in revenue was driven by heightened demand for air cargo, particularly for the transport of high-value and time-sensitive goods, as well as the expansion of its freighter fleet and cargo terminal capacity, said MMAG.
Its mobile and fulfillment logistics segment also contributed positively, buoyed by strong demand for smart devices and information technology hardware.
On the back of higher capacity utilisation and improved unit economics, MMAG narrowed its pre-tax loss by 19.2 per cent to RM83.50 million for FP26, compared to a pre-tax loss of RM103.33 million previously.
Gross profit turned around significantly to RM80.41 million, compared to a gross loss of RM25.37 million in the prior period.
The proposed capital reduction is not contingent on any other corporate exercises but requires the approval of shareholders via a special resolution at an upcoming extraordinary general meeting.
Barring unforeseen circumstances, the corporate exercise is expected to be completed in the first quarter of 2027.

Title: Pos Malaysia powers up EV deliveries with 1,585 'green' vehicles
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pos Malaysia Bhd says it now delivers one in three parcels using electric vehicles (EVs), as it accelerates the shift towards lower-carbon last-mile delivery
The national postal and parcel operator boasts the country's largest electric logistics fleet, comprising 1,253 electric motorcycles and 332 electric vans across Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak.
Since 2023, its EV fleet has travelled 28.8 million kilometres, equivalent to about 719 trips around the world, while helping avoid an estimated 3,881 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (CO₂e) emissions.
Pos Malaysia said the scale of its electrification programme demonstrates how sustainable logistics can be integrated into everyday parcel delivery without changing the way customers send or receive parcels.
The company is also using technology to improve the efficiency of its fleet, with more than 2,200 vehicles equipped with telematics.
The technology provides operational data to optimise delivery routes, improve driver safety and increase fleet utilisation, while supporting continuous improvements across its nationwide network.
The initiative is featured in a Sustainability Impact Case Study developed with the United Nations Global Compact Network Malaysia, Brunei and Cambodia (UNGCMBC).
The study examines Pos Malaysia's approach to combining EVs, charging infrastructure, telematics, capital planning and workforce readiness to transform its delivery operations.
Group chief executive officer Charles Brewer said fleet electrification was a key part of the company's sustainability and decarbonisation strategy.
"Today, we operate Malaysia's largest electric fleet, delivering mail and parcels across the country," he said.
Brewer said the initiative supports Pos Malaysia's ambition to achieve 100 per cent green deliveries by 2030 and net Zero by 2050.
"The priority now is to keep scaling what works - integrating the vehicles, associated infrastructure, data and people to make lower-carbon delivery the core of how we operate," he said.
The company said the transition is aimed at building a smarter, cleaner and more resilient logistics network as parcel volumes and customer expectations continue to evolve.

Title: Sultan Ibrahim consents to new Pulau Aur mosque being used for Friday prayers
Article:
JOHOR BARU: His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, has consented to the newly completed mosque on Pulau Aur being used for Friday prayers for the first time.
According to a post on Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar's official Facebook page today, His Majesty also consented to the mosque being named Masjid Zuhri.
It said the mosque, which can accommodate nearly 200 congregants, was rebuilt after its previous structure deteriorated over the years, including roof leaks.
"The remote location of Pulau Aur also made it difficult for local residents to carry out repair works on the mosque.
"As such, Teto Engineering Sdn Bhd provided waqf funding for the reconstruction of the mosque to provide a more comfortable and suitable place of worship for residents of Pulau Aur and surrounding areas," it said.
Earlier, Sultan Ibrahim granted an audience to Johor Mufti Datuk Yahya Ahmad at Istana Pasir Pelangi here.
His Majesty was also briefed by Yahya on matters concerning Islamic affairs in Johor.
Also present were Johor Islamic Religious Council chief executive officer Datuk Mohd Radzi Mohd Amin and Teto Engineering Sdn Bhd chairman Datuk Mohd Zuhri Abdullah.

Title: Mihas 2026 targets RM5bil sales
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The 22nd Malaysia International Halal Showcase (Mihas 2026) is targeting RM5 billion in total sales value, with 50,000 visitors expected to attend the four-day event.
Opening tomorrow at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre, Mihas 2026 will bring together 1,700 companies across 2,000 exhibition booths.
Malaysia External Trade Development Corp chief executive officer Datuk Abu Bakar Yusof said the event will provide a dedicated AI agent and personalised support to participants to discover businesses, engage with exhibitors and build relevant connections.
"We believe this approach will enhance the Mihas experience and support our efforts to achieve RM5 billion in sales value this year," he said in a statement.
The exhibition will serve as a commercial hub for the global halal economy, connecting international suppliers, trade buyers and industry leaders.
Mihas' flagship business matching programme, the international sourcing programme, is expected to facilitate 4,000 meetings between 450 international buyers, including 50 premium buyers, with around 600 Malaysian exporters.
The programme is expected to contribute significantly to the exhibition's overall trade target.
Additionally, the Women in Export Forum has expanded into a dedicated pavilion featuring 80 booths inspired by women entrepreneurs in the halal industry, comprising 60 Malaysian and 20 international exhibitors.
Other attractions include daily runway presentations showcasing modest-fashion trends and live culinary demonstrations at the Mihas Kitchen.

Title: Anwar arrives in Shanghai for 3-day China working visit
Article:
SHANGHAI: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim arrived here today for a three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou aimed at strengthening Malaysia-China ties, boosting trade and expanding cooperation in emerging technologies.
The aircraft carrying Anwar and his delegation landed at Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport at 5.10pm local time (5.10pm Malaysian time).
He was welcomed by Malaysian Ambassador to China Datuk Norman Muhamad and Consul General of Malaysia in Shanghai Abdullah Ma'amor Ibrahim.
Also present were Shanghai Vice-Mayor Wang Huajie, China's Ambassador to Malaysia Ouyang Yujing and Su Lin, a member of the Party Leadership Group of the Shanghai Municipal Foreign Affairs Office.
The visit, at the invitation of the Chinese government, is Anwar's 4th to China since he became prime minister in 2022.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, is accompanied by Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
The highlight of the visit will be Anwar's high-level meeting with Chinese Premier Li Qiang in Hangzhou, the capital of Zhejiang province, on Thursday.
In Shanghai, Anwar is scheduled to attend WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 at the National Exhibition and Convention Center (NECC), where he will deliver a keynote address at the plenary session of the WorldSkills Conference 2026 tomorrow.
He will also attend the 5th Global Digital Trade Expo in Hangzhou, where Malaysia and Hungary are participating as Guest Countries of Honour.
Anwar is scheduled to deliver a keynote address at the expo, one of China's major digital economy platforms, highlighting artificial intelligence (AI) and global cooperation.
During the visit, Anwar is also expected to engage Chinese industry leaders in a roundtable session and hold one-on-one meetings with key industry and technology companies to drive foreign direct investment into Malaysia.
China has remained Malaysia's largest trading partner for 17 consecutive years, with total bilateral trade reaching US$113.82 billion (RM456.68 billion) between January and August this year.

Title: Israel minister vows to force out all of Gaza City if any Israeli abducted
Article:
TEL AVIV: Israel's defence minister vowed Tuesday to force out all of Gaza City's residents and displace a million people in the war-ravaged territory if any Israeli is abducted in the future.
Speaking at a memorial for the 1973 Yom Kippur War, Defence Minister Israel Katz also threatened the destruction of infrastructure, which, like the forced displacement of civilians, constitutes a war crime under the Geneva Conventions.
"I hereby warn the terrorist organisation and its supporters, from Iran to Erdogan – if a single Israeli soldier or civilian is kidnapped, the entire city of Gaza, with its houses and terror towers, will be evacuated southward with its million residents," Katz said, referring to Hamas and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, an outspoken critic of Israel's Gaza campaign.
"This is the language that the jihadist terrorist organisations in Gaza and Lebanon understand, and this is the language we speak – evacuation of the population, destruction of infrastructure and taking over the territory," he said, also referring to Lebanese Shia movement Hizbollah.
Gaza City is home to around 1.1 million people, according to the municipality. The entire Gaza Strip has some two million people, who after nearly three years of war have been packed into the 30 per cent of the territory not controlled by Israel.
Hamas on Oct 7, 2023 led the deadliest attack ever against Israel in which militants killed 1,221 people and dragged into Gaza some 251 hostages, 44 of them already dead, according to Israeli official figures.
Israel launched a massive retaliatory offensive that has displaced virtually the entire population at least once and has killed 73,919 people, according to the Gaza health ministry, whose figures are generally considered reliable.
Katz, known for his outspoken remarks, recently said that Israel agreed to an Oct 2025 US-brokered ceasefire declaration only to free the remaining hostages and that he expected Israel, which has kept up strikes at a lower pace, to return to full-scale war in Gaza.
The comments come ahead of Oct 27 elections in which Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is facing criticism from the opposition that he failed both to prevent the attack and to deliver military success afterwards.
In his latest remarks, Katz again also threatened to return to war with Iran, whose cleric-run government supports Hamas.
"The work is not yet finished and if we need to, we will strike a third time until the terrorist regime is overthrown and eliminated," Katz said.
The United States and Israel jointly attacked Iran in late February, with an initial Israeli strike killing supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
Israel halted its campaign in April after US President Donald Trump entered a ceasefire and sought a negotiated settlement to the war, which has sharply raised oil prices and been highly unpopular among US voters.

Title: Selangor Malay Reserve Land up 1,084.55 hectares since 2018, says Amirudin
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 22 — The total area of Malay Reserve Land in Selangor has increased by 1,084.55 hectares (2,680 acres) since 2018, said Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
In a statement today, Amirudin said the overall area under the state government’s administration had increased from 162,161.98 hectares (400,711 acres) to 163,246.54 hectares (403,391 acres).

He added that to balance local development with the interests of Malay Reserve Land, a separate 22.41-hectare plot of land in Hulu Selangor was concurrently undergoing the gazetting process as Malay Reserve Land.

Title: Just 40m long, new Mont Kiara road opens shortcut to Solaris and Segambut
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — A new road measuring just 40 metres has opened in Mont Kiara, creating a direct connection between Jalan Duta Kiara and Jalan Kiara 3 and giving motorists an alternative route towards Solaris Dutamas, Segambut and surrounding areas.
The RM3 million two-way link, fully funded by developer Bon Estates as part of its corporate social responsibility programme, is expected to reduce lengthy detours for residents in the densely developed neighbourhood, the
New Straits Times
reported.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said Jalan Duta Kiara had previously ended in a dead end, forcing motorists travelling between Bukit Pelangi and Solaris to take a longer route despite the two areas being close to one another.
“Before this road was constructed, those from Bukit Pelangi wanting to go to Solaris could not simply cross over despite the areas being so close.
“Everybody had to be stuck in the traffic. For residents here, they had to make a big round just to get home.
“With this connection, you can turn left or right, while traffic from the other side can come straight through,” she was quoted as saying after opening the road today.
Yeoh said the project followed discussions involving the developer, the Mont Kiara Residents’ Association and other local stakeholders over traffic and connectivity concerns in the area.
“I am very happy with the process of engagement with the stakeholders. This is how every development should be.
“You hear the feedback from the member of parliament, engage the local residents’ association and meet the needs of the local community,” she said.
According to the report, the new route would also provide another option for motorists travelling near a school along the existing road network.
Yeoh said Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) was also planning another road connection from Jalan Kiara 7 to the Sprint Highway via the Penchala Link, which would further expand access in Mont Kiara.
“Mont Kiara has about 50 condominiums. I cannot undo the development because it was already like that when I was elected.
“But over the last few years, we have worked very hard with private developers and DBKL to facilitate the opening of more roads and give people greater access,” she said.
Yeoh said congestion and limited road connectivity remained among the main concerns raised by residents, particularly those travelling between neighbouring residential and commercial areas.
There is currently no estimate of how many vehicles are expected to use the new connection, she added, noting that DBKL had to balance infrastructure spending across different parliamentary constituencies.

Title: MCMC ready to license e-commerce platforms once ministries set conditions, says deputy minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — The Communications Ministry is waiting for the terms and conditions from the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) and the Finance Ministry (MoF) before licensing e-commerce platforms.
Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has the power under the existing legal framework to license the platforms, but the specific conditions must be decided by the relevant ministries.
“Yes, we actually had a discussion with the MOF together with KPDN. I think KPDN’s decision is to study how to regulate these e-commerce platforms. MCMC, or the Ministry of Communications, is involved because under the Malaysian legal framework, we have the power to actually license e-commerce platforms.
“However, we are waiting for instructions or feedback from MoF, (and) especially from KPDN, on the terms and conditions to be imposed,” she told reporters after attending the media launch of the Asean-China Cross Border E-Commerce Expo 2026 (CBE2026) at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre (KLCC) here today.
Teo said MCMC was ready to implement the licensing once the framework was in place to ensure a fair business environment.
She was responding to growing concerns among local retailers over the presence of a major China-based e-commerce platform known for its ultra-low-cost products.
“MCMC is ready anytime. We have engaged with the platform as well, but again, this is not just targeting it, but all e-commerce platforms. We want to level the playing field and make sure that Malaysian consumers are protected,” she said.
Meanwhile, when asked about DAP secretary-general and Transport Minister Anthony Loke’s offer to resign, Teo said the party’s Central Executive Committee (CEC) had decided that all its ministers and deputy ministers would remain in their respective positions.
She said their continued presence in the Cabinet was a strong testament to their unwavering support for Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s leadership. — Bernama

Title: Magnitude 4.4 earthquake detected off Batu Pahat, tremors felt onshore
Article:
BATU PAHAT, Sept 22 — A magnitude 4.4 earthquake was detected off the coast of Batu Pahat at 4.55pm today.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said the earthquake struck at a depth of 10 kilometres, with its epicentre at 1.7 degrees north and 102.7 degrees east, about 27 kilometres southwest of Batu Pahat.
Tremors were felt in Batu Pahat and surrounding areas, MetMalaysia said, adding that it would continue to monitor the situation. — Bernama

Article:

The notification was dated September 10 and signed by the Secretary of the DUN Sarawak.
Asked whether any Bills, particularly important ones, would be tabled during the sitting, Asfia said his office had yet to receive any Bills from the state government.
